title: GPX Reverse Track Tool: Run It Backwards
description: Reverse a GPX track's direction with the GPX Reverse Track Tool — start becomes finish, segment by segment, locally. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, yesterday's point-to-point hike from the valley town to the high bothy reverses into tomorrow's file: bothy to town, every bend in mirror order, ready to load before you set off.
quick_answer: The GPX Reverse Track Tool flips each track segment in a GPX file so the route runs from its former finish back to its start. Load the file locally and download the reversed copy — the same path re-ordered, for return journeys and reverse riding.
steps_intro: The same path, walked the other way:

body.t: Point-to-point routes rarely retrace themselves in your library. Reverse the outbound file and the return leg has its own navigable track.

use_cases.title: Riding the route the other way

body.t: Trail direction changes a ride completely — climbs become descents. Reversing lets you preview the mirrored day, and the
on the reversed file re-prices the effort.
A track stitched or exported in reverse order confuses every downstream tool. Reversing restores the true direction of travel.
Events that alternate direction yearly need both editions of the course file — one reversal apart.

Within each segment, the point order inverts: last becomes first. Segments themselves stay in place (segment 1 remains segment 1) — the tool mirrors journeys, it does not reshuffle a multi-leg day into nonsense.
A route that gained 48 m and lost 8 becomes, reversed, a route that gains 8 and loses 48 — the identity gain − loss flips sign with the direction, exactly as the ground would.

popular_table.title: Reversal semantics
popular_table.intro: Precisely what changes — and the one thing to think about (time).
rows: Tracks are the subject; standalone waypoints are untouched
Identical — the path is the same set of segments
popular_table.note: A reversed track is a plan for travelling the path backwards — treat its numbers as the mirror day's, and re-derive anything time-of-day dependent (shade, tides, shop hours) from the new direction.

faq: Does reversing change the shape or distance?
No — the polyline is identical, only its direction of travel flips. Any distance tool reads the same total from either edition.
They mirror: the profile chart reads right-to-left compared to the original, gains and losses swap roles, and the max elevation stays the same mountain.
Each segment reverses internally while segment order is preserved — a multi-leg recording stays a coherent set, each leg individually mirrored.
Can I reverse a route (<rte>) too?
This tool's subject is tracks. Planned routes reverse in route planners; the geometry principle is identical if your editor offers it.
Will my device follow a reversed track?
Devices follow point order — the reversed file navigates finish-to-start exactly as the original navigated start-to-finish.
Track names ride along unchanged — rename the copy (…-reversed) so your library does not confuse the two directions at 6 a.m.
